title: When the tongue keeps outrunning the soul
issueStatement: Words are arriving faster than remembrance, so speech starts leaving damage before wisdom enters the room.
centralInsight: Gurbani disciplines speech through Naam, humility, and praise. The tongue becomes trustworthy when it no longer serves ego, impulse, or spiritual theatre.
practicalReflection: Speech reveals the state of the inner room. A clean tongue is not produced by technique alone; it comes from a heart slowed enough to speak under guidance.
actionPrompt: Before the next unnecessary word, ask whether it will leave the room cleaner, truer, and more peaceful.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: When pressure makes the tongue want relief
pressure.issueStatement: The room is tight, the body is hot, and speech starts reaching for instant relief: sharpness, accusation, performance, or control. Under strain, the tongue wants to spend pain outward.
pressure.centralInsight: Gurbani disciplines speech most severely when pressure would excuse it. Clean speech under strain is not softness without truth; it is truth delivered without ego asking the tongue to do its violence for it.
pressure.practicalReflection: Pressure reveals whether speech is serving clarity or discharge. The sentence you most want to say quickly is often the one that needs the most gurmat before release.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: When speech keeps outrunning wisdom after the slip
repair.issueStatement: Words are arriving faster than remembrance, so speech starts leaving damage before wisdom enters the room. The break has already happened, and now the temptation is to hide, explain, harden, or turn the miss into identity.
repair.centralInsight: Gurbani disciplines speech through Naam, humility, and praise. The tongue becomes trustworthy when it no longer serves ego, impulse, or spiritual theatre. After the miss, Gurbani keeps the way back near humility, truthfulness, and the next faithful act.
repair.practicalReflection: Repair after speech damage becomes real when the tongue stops protecting its image and starts cleaning what it harmed. A brief, honest return is usually stronger than a long defense of why the words came out that way.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: When speech needs a rule before it becomes clean
practice.issueStatement: Words keep escaping faster than awareness. Good intentions are not enough; without discipline, the tongue keeps returning to the same old routes.
practice.centralInsight: Gurbani does not clean speech by inspiration alone. It trains restraint, remembrance, and accountability until the tongue learns that not every impulse deserves a voice.
practice.practicalReflection: Speech changes when it is given a rule. A practiced boundary can do more for the soul than a hundred moments of regret after damage is already done.
practice.actionPrompt: For the next seven days, keep one speech discipline: do not speak about an absent person unless it is necessary, true, and clean.
